# Savings

Savings is where you watch the money your future self has set aside actually add up.
Every time your spending accrues a self-tax and you move that money into your savings
account, it lands here — so the tax you impose on yourself stops being an abstract
number and becomes a balance you can see growing.

## What you've set aside

The top of the page is the headline: how much you've set aside so far, sat next to two
figures that give it meaning.

- **Owed to your future self** — the total tax you've had levied across all your
  weeks. This is the target: what your savings are working toward.
- **Coverage** — how much of that you've actually funded. When you're fully caught up,
  coverage reads full; when you're behind, it tells you by how much. Until any tax has
  been levied there's nothing to cover, so it simply shows a dash rather than a
  misleading zero.

The numbers count up as the page settles, so the balance reads as something that
moves, not a static figure printed on a card.

## Where the balance came from

Below the headline is a simple split of what built your savings:

- **Gained from self-tax** — the money the self-tax mechanism set aside for you,
  automatically, as you spent.
- **Surplus you added** — anything you chose to move into savings on top of that,
  ahead of any bill.

For most people, early on, it's all self-tax, so this reads as a single bar — the
mechanism quietly doing its job. The moment you top it up yourself, the second part
appears, so you can always tell how much of your savings you built by habit versus by
choice.

## Your trend over time

Last is the trend — your running savings balance week by week, so you can see the line
climb. It's the long view: not "how much this week" but "how far this has come." Over a
few months it turns a series of small weekly set-asides into a visible, growing total.

## Why it's called Savings

Right now this is exactly what the name says: real money, set aside, yours. It's built
to be the home for more than that over time — the place your set-aside balance can
eventually be put to work — but everything you see here today is straightforward
savings you've provisioned for yourself.
